title: Protocol for high-throughput single-cell patterning using a reusable ultrathin metal microstencil
protocol: Fix and load the UTmS chip for SEM imaging.
Fix the UTmS-chip on a metal tray with conductive tape.
Bring the SEM chamber to atmospheric pressure to open the sample door.
Open the door and place the metal tray into the holder.
Close the door back into the chamber and place it back under vacuum.
Zoom in to the desired magnification and adjust the sample height to focus.
Capture the SEM image once the sample is in focus.
Bend the UTmS chip without fracturing or creasing using fingers.
Place the cleaned and sterilized UTmS chip in a Petri dish.
Co-culture MCF-7 cells with the UTmS chip for 3 days in an incubator.
Prepare substrates with clean and planar top surfaces.
Peel off a freshly-prepared PDMS layer without patterns using tweezers.
Paste the uncovered fresh side of the PDMS towards the substrate's top surface gradually to remove air bubbles.
Prepare a fibronectin coating solution with a final concentration of 5 μg/mL using PBS in Eppendorf tubes with sufficient mixing in a biosafety cabinet.
Store excess fibronectin solutions at 4°C.
Extend pipetting time to achieve maximum dissolution and mixing for fibronectin.
Prepare a mixed coating solution including human fibronectin and fibrinogen in PBS.
Vortex the mixed coating solution for 5 s.
Pipette the fibronectin solution into the PDMS gasket.
Incubate the surfaces at 36°C for a minimum of 3 h or at 4°C for 10 h.
Cover the dish with aluminum foil to prevent liquid evaporation during incubation.
Remove the soaking solution after incubation.
Gently wash the Petri dish with PBS using a pipette to remove unbound fibronectin.
Do not allow the pipette tip to touch the base when aspirating the fibronectin solution or washing with PBS to avoid damaging the protein layer.
Blow-dry the residues with nitrogen gas until a white crystalline layer appears.
Apply nitrogen gas at a distance of at least 30 cm from the substrate to prevent rapid airflow from damaging the protein layer.
Carefully check the protein layer on the surface during the blowing process and stop as soon as it becomes white to prevent overdrying.
Store the fibronectin-modified chips at 4°C for up to one week until subsequent device assembly.
Perform AFM measurements in dry mode using an AFM (Bruker Multimode V, Germany).
Attach the fibronectin-coated PDMS membrane on a glass slide.
Place the prepared glass slide in the AFM sample stage.
Place a probe in the AFM and activate the laser and photodetector.
Use a cantilever with Bruker DNP10 (silicon nitride with elastic coefficient of 0.6N/m).
Scan the boundary of the fibronectin area in Scanasyst air mode.
Create an AFM image of the surface line by line.
Place the clean UTmS-chips using tweezers at the center of the freshly prepared culture dish or PDMS layer at ambient temperatures and under atmospheric pressure.
Gently press on the UTmS with the finger to ensure tight contact with the substrate surface.
Load with sustaining liquid without floating and leakage.
Ensure the use of clean and sterile gloves before pressing the UTmS with the finger.
Press the central area first and then extend to the edges because the through-hole array is in the center of the UTmS chip.
Dispense Cy3 solution on the center of the UTmS surface, which remains in a droplet shape due to hydrophobicity.
Observe green fluorescence of the Cy3 droplet from the backside of the assembled UTmS-chip using an inverted fluorescence microscope equipped with 10× and 20× objective lenses and a camera.
Cut the UTmS-Chip in half to observe the longitudinal section of the through-holes area.
Prepare cell suspensions at a density of 1 × 10^6–3 × 10^6 cells per mL and mix thoroughly for subsequent cell loading.
Pipette a drop of the cell-suspended medium onto the stencil region of the UTmS-chip to cover the stencil array.
Transfer the chip to a CO2 incubator at 37°C for 20 min to allow the cells to attach to the fibronectin-modified substrate under gravity-induced natural sedimentation.
Gently aspirate the cells suspension before peeling the UTmS layer.
Rinse with a warm medium to remove unattached cells.
Peel off the UTmS from the substrate using tweezers, starting from one corner.
Rinse with a warm medium to remove extra cells attached to single-point cell patterns.
Recover the single-cell array with fresh culture medium after peel-off process.
Incubate in an incubator for another 20 min.
Immerse the single-cell array in PBS.
Prepare the staining solution of FDA and Hoechst33342.
Mix 4 μL FDA (5 mg/mL) with 2 μL Hoechst solution (10 mg/mL) in 2 mL complete culture medium.
Maintain the staining solution in dark conditions.
Gently aspirate PBS from the assembled dish.
Slowly add 2 mL of the staining solution into the Petri dish to immerse the cells.
Transfer the device into a CO2 incubator at 37°C for 10 min.
Remove the staining solution after incubation.
Rinse the dish twice with PBS.
Image the single-cell array using an inverted fluorescence microscope in dark conditions.
Prepare the mixed reagent for cell apoptosis characterization.
Add 8 μL TMRM (100 μM) and 20 μL of STS apoptosis inducer (1 mM) to 2 mL complete culture medium.
Mix thoroughly and maintain the solution in the dark.
Image a single-cell array using a Cy3 filter cube and 10× objective on an inverted fluorescence microscope equipped with temperature, humidity, and CO2 control for apoptosis assays.
Turn on the microscope at least 1 hour before use.
Set the heating unit temperature to 37°C.
Place the assembled dish in the plate holder.
Immerse the single-cell array in PBS slowly.
Add 2 mL of mixed reagent containing 10 μM STS to a 3.5-cm Petri dish.
Prepare a control group without STS.
Select positions to record using the software interface.
Adjust focus, exposure time, light power, and acquisition rate.
Start imaging the single-cell array every 10 minutes for 4 hours.
Use ImageJ to measure gray values of red fluorescence images of individual cells.
Prepare 1× loading solution of Ca2+ indicator dye (Fluo-8 no wash calcium assay kit) with Fluo-8 stock solution and 1× assay buffer.
Mix thoroughly and maintain the solution in the dark.
Construct three single MCF-7 cell arrays in a 10 × 20 array with the UTmS-chip and independently incubate for 1 h with 1 ml Fluo-8 dye-loading solution.
Protect the entire process from light.
Add 100 μL KCl solutions of 0, 100, and 200 mM to stimulate the individual cells in the three assembled devices.
Turn on the microscope, camera, CO2 supply, water pump, and heating unit at least 1 hour before use.
Set the heating unit temperature to 37°C.
Place the assembled dish with a single MCF-7 cell arrays in a 10 × 20 array in the plate holder.
Slowly aspirate the PBS covering the single-cell array.
Add Fluo-8 dye-loading solution for a 3.5-cm Petri dish.
Incubate the cells for 1 hour in dark conditions.
Slowly add 100 μL KCl solution to stimulate the single cells in the assembled device.
Select the positions to record using the software interface.
Adjust the focus, exposure time, light power, time length of the acquisition, and acquisition rate.
Start imaging the single-cell array.
Keep parameters constant throughout the observation period.
Use ImageJ to measure the gray values of the green fluorescence images of individual cells taken at 5-min intervals.
Acquire boxplots of single-cell assay data using Origin (2018 version).
Create real-time plots of the normalized fluorescence intensity of individual cells as a function of culture time using Origin (2018 version).
Peel off the UTmS after single-cell patterning and immerse it in a dish or tube with trypsin at 37°C for 10 min.
Remove the UTmS with tweezers and rinse with DI water.
Place the UTmS in a clean dish or tube with ethanol and then ultrasonically clean for 10 min.
If necessary, use a water bath at 65°C to aid in ultrasonic cleaning of dirty chips.
Wash the UTmS thoroughly with DI water to remove ethanol residues, and dry using nitrogen gas.
Sterilize the stencil using UV-ozone disinfector for 30 min.
Optionally, sterilize the stencil through vacuum vapor sterilization.
Place the UTmS under backlight observation to verify clean through holes.
Use an inverted microscope to visually confirm that no defects are present in the through-hole array of cleaned stencils.
Place the cleaned UTmS-chips in a 35-mm sterilized Petri dish without fixation.
Seal the Petri dish with parafilm and store the UTmS-chips in a vacuum desiccator for extended periods.
Optionally, store UTmS-chips in a Gel-box with a polymer silicone layer to ensure chip tile is fixed on the bottom.
